summary: @servicetitan/toolbelt-shared-registry preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (bun-v1.3.13) into a temp directory, unzips it, chmods it executable, and then invokes the freshly downloaded Bun binary against a local file math_init.js. math_init.js is a single-line, 727KB, obfuscator.io-style bundle (rotated string array via function WV8StW, hex-mangled identifiers, no imports, no human-readable strings) with a '// @bun @bun-cjs' header, so it can only run under Bun rather than Node. The filename has no relation to the package's advertised purpose (a small React IoC registry, whose actual code lives unrelated in dist/index.js). Fetching a second alternate runtime at install specifically to execute a heavily obfuscated payload is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to evade Node-oriented install-time scanners. The scoped-vendor name (@servicetitan) combined with install-time delivery of unrelated obfuscated code is consistent with a namespace compromise or typosquat against the ServiceTitan scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
